A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ReSA research. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete Appendices A-C support comparison, including material relocated in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original ReSA classification, transfer-learning, clustering, low-shot, and ablation results in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds results from pretraining on long-tailed CIFAR-100 in Appendix C.3 and Figure 12.

M1.justification: The loss, Sinkhorn procedure, augmentation design, and Appendix B pseudocode are unchanged. Renaming Representation Soft Assignment to Representation Self-Assignment and replacing similarity-matrix shorthand with explicit matrix products do not change the method.

E1.justification: Appendix C.3 adds CIFAR100-LT pretraining, introducing a class-imbalanced training distribution with evaluation on the full CIFAR-100 test set. All previously evaluated datasets and tasks remain.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in the corresponding existing tables and analyses. The new long-tailed experiment uses MoCoV3, INTL, and VICReg, all already evaluated against ReSA in v1.

E3.justification: The added long-tailed experiment specifies an imbalance factor of 1/20, 15,907 training images, ResNet-18 pretraining for 1,000 epochs, and linear-probe and k-NN evaluation on the full CIFAR-100 test set. Existing experimental protocols remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New Appendix C.3 and Figure 12 examine convergence and representation quality under class imbalance, addressing whether early clustering errors persist during learning. The existing architecture, temperature, augmentation, and encoding-versus-embedding ablations are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The new experiment adds trajectories without uncertainty bands; the existing SC standard deviation remains a metric across data points, not uncertainty across training runs.

E6.justification: The contents and numerical values of Tables 1-12 are unchanged. New Figure 12 reports losses and classification trajectories under long-tailed pretraining: ReSA improves more slowly initially but ultimately leads MoCoV3, INTL, and VICReg in k-NN top-1 and linear top-1/top-5 accuracy.

T1.justification: Section 4.2 adds explicit similarity-gradient derivations for InfoNCE and ReSA, including the ReSA gradient (P_ij - A_H,ij)/tau. Appendix C.2 adds a mathematical argument for diagonal assignment dominance based on asserted Sinkhorn monotonicity. Together these substantially expand the mathematical account of optimization and collapse avoidance beyond v1.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: superior clustering properties of encodings, ReSA's positive-feedback learning framework, strong benchmark performance, and fine- and coarse-grained representation quality. The method's expanded name changes, but these claims do not.

C2.justification: v2 expands explanations of projector information loss, optimization with soft assignments, and avoidance of early clustering errors. It interprets the new long-tailed trajectories as possible recovery from noisy initial clusters. Appendix B.2 also removes v1's explicit statement that computational resources limited ViT hyperparameter tuning.

D1.justification: Appendix C.3 supplies a source reference and construction, training, and evaluation details for CIFAR100-LT. Existing implementation pseudocode, optimizer and evaluation parameters, hardware disclosures, and code-access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds Jing et al. (2022), Wang and Isola (2020), and Bizeul et al. (2024), while removing the He et al. (2022) masked-autoencoder citation. Sections 2.2 and 4.2 provide more focused positioning around information loss and theoretical analyses of contrastive learning.

P1.justification: v2 renames ReSA, rewrites Section 2.2, inserts the gradient subsection and long-tailed appendix subsection, and updates subsequent numbering and author/publication text. Most experimental prose, contribution statements, and existing appendix material retain their wording and organization.

P2.justification: v2 adds the seven-panel Figure 12 and relocates existing displays, including Figures 3-4 and Table 4. Existing plots and table structures are retained, with limited caption changes and a reformatted author block.

improvement.justification: The long-tailed experiment adds a relevant stress test absent from v1, and Section 4.2 clarifies optimization with soft assignments while existing results remain intact. These provide a limited net improvement. However, Appendix C.2's new ordering-preservation claim is not generally valid under Algorithm 1's unequal column rescaling, weakening the added mathematical explanation of collapse avoidance.
